title: Declarative workflow graph v1
description: The workflow as data: steps, transitions, guards with their authority, caps and recovery targets. Closed: unknown fields and unknown versions fail. Duplicate keys are refused by the parser before this schema runs, because a parsed object no longer carries them.

entry_steps.description: Every other step the graph may be entered at, and why. A graph that registers one workflow entered one way needs only first_step; the autosk-flow graph registers eight workflows, and its daemon also enters two repair steps out of band when a snapshot or the authority journal fails revalidation. Reachability is judged from first_step together with these, because a step entered this way is not orphaned.

reason.description: Why the graph is entered here, stated so an entry cannot be added without saying what enters it.

graph_reasons.description: Refusals the graph itself issues, which no edge or step can carry: an undeclared pair has no edge and therefore no guard.

transition_not_declared.description: Pinned to its own code: this contract owns it, so a document that renamed it would be naming a refusal nothing closes.

resume_target_not_permitted.description: Pinned to its own code, for the same reason.

predicates.description: The closed enumeration a guard may reference. An expression language was rejected: it would need its own specification, parser and mutation coverage, and the cost of an error here is a silently permitted transition.

reads.description: The recorded state this predicate inspects. Named so that a predicate cannot quietly widen what it looks at.

status.description: Present exactly when kind is status: the task status this terminal or parking step drives.

hooks.description: Which optional agent hooks the step declares. Hook presence is declared structure; hook bodies are code and belong to the distribution digest.

no_transition_reason.description: The reason the flow parks at this step when no outgoing edge is a candidate. Required for a non-terminal step; a step that can neither leave nor say why it did not leave is refused.

then.description: A status step neither runs nor explains a failure to leave, so it carries no hooks and no no_transition_reason. Written as a narrowed property set rather than a negation: the shared Schema engine implements the positive keywords only.
An agent step drives no task status of its own, so status is absent and the reason for parking is mandatory.

guards.description: A guard is the condition. There is no second mechanism: a transition names the guards bound to it, and their conjunction is what must hold. Two alternative paths are two edges, not a disjunction. Bounded by the transition count rather than by the predicate count, because that rule is what makes guards multiply: one guard exists per alternative per edge, so a graph may declare more guards than it declares distinct conditions.

predicate.description: An id from the predicates enumeration. An unknown id fails closed.

park_reason.description: The reason named when this guard refuses an explicitly requested target. Selection does not park on a false guard; it disqualifies the edge.

priority.description: Among candidate edges out of one step the lowest priority wins. Two edges leaving one step with equal priority is a schema error rather than a runtime choice, so the outcome is decided by data and not by enumeration order.

caps.description: A cap counts the taking of one named transition and nothing else, so a retry after a tool or provider failure is not a round.

counted_transition.description: The transition id whose taking increments the counter.

limit.description: The shipped limit. A user decision may authorise exceeding it for one epic and scope; that authorisation is a decision record and not an edit here, so it does not move the digest.

recovery.description: One row per park reason. parks_at is where the flow stops with it: the steps the graph parks it from, plus the status step a parked task stands on. handled_at is the rest of the steps the row names, where the reason is dealt with and where resume leaves from but where the graph never raises it. resume_targets is where the user may resume.

parks_at.description: Exactly where the graph parks this reason, plus any status step a parked task stands on. What the graph produces is the step an edge leaves, so it names a park's origin and never its landing, which is the one thing it cannot check here. Everything else is checked in both directions. Bounded by the step count rather than by a smaller guess: one reason can name 68 steps across this field and handled_at together.

handled_at.description: The steps this row names that the graph never parks the reason at: where it is dealt with, and where resume leaves from. Optional, because 61 of the 84 rows name none, and the widest holds 46 of project_boundary_invalid's 68. Bounded by the step count for the same reason as parks_at.

resume_targets.description: Every entry must be a declared edge from one of this reason's parks_at or handled_at steps. A target outside that union is refused with graph_reasons.resume_target_not_permitted. Bounded by the step count for the same reason as parks_at.

views.description: The rendered tables this document is the source of. A view is written here rather than derived from `recovery` because the rendered unit is the row, not the reason: rows group several reasons behind one cell, one reason appears in several rows under different qualifiers, and one view names its reasons in prose rather than in codes. `rows` is order-carrying — the order is the table. Every code a view's rows cover, taken together, must be exactly the set `recovery` declares, which is what makes the two tables one truth rather than two that agree today.

renders_into.description: The repository-relative file the view is rendered into. The header line locates it there.

rule.description: The separator line under the header, carried so the render is the file's bytes and not this contract's idea of them.

coverage.description: Whether the view is the whole enumeration or a part of it. `complete` must cover every reason `recovery` declares. `partial` must name every reason it leaves out, so a reason cannot quietly stop being explained: dropping one takes an edit to `omits` that a reviewer sees.

omits.description: Present exactly when coverage is partial: the reasons this view deliberately does not explain. Covered and omitted together must be exactly what `recovery` declares.

covers.description: The park reasons this row is about. Empty is legal and means the row explains something the vocabulary does not name.

binds.description: sha256 over the canonical form of the recovery entries this row explains, sorted by reason. Covering the whole entry rather than the reason names is what makes a changed resume rule oblige a look at the sentence explaining it: the names alone stayed valid while the rule underneath them was rewritten.

else.description: A complete view leaves nothing out, so it carries no omissions list. Narrowed property set rather than a negation, as elsewhere in this schema.

canonical_digest.description: sha256 over the canonical serialization of this document with this field removed, not over the committed file bytes.

name.description: A step or workflow name. Compared against the daemon under its own rule, so the character set is deliberately narrow.

park_reason.description: A code the refusal vocabulary owns. A guard naming a code outside it is refused by the validator.

authority.description: Who may take the transition. Criterion 2 names five components and none of them says who is entitled to act; this is where that lives, inside guards rather than as a sixth component.

policy_rules.description: Present exactly when actor is policy: the classifier rule ids the authorisation is bound to.

policy_scope.description: Present exactly when actor is policy: the recorded bounds the authorisation may not exceed.

else.description: A human or agent authority carries no policy binding, so both policy fields are absent. Narrowed property set for the same reason as the step branches above.
